characterization_methods.key_findings: 9Al-20Mn-1C after 800 °C tempering measured 249 HV (Table 8), softer than its 600 °C tempered value (359 HV) and only slightly harder than its hot-rolled value (233 HV).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 kg load for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample; data consistency checked with Minitab18® (outliers excluded)
characterization_methods.purpose: Compare the hardness of the hot-rolled and heat-treated (600 °C and 800 °C tempered) conditions of the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural analysis of all alloys at the different processing conditions (hot-rolling and tempering).

analytical_models.equation_role: thermodynamic calculation of equilibrium phase amounts to assess the gradient in austenite stability between hot-rolling (1150 °C) and tempering (800 °C)
analytical_models.model_note: Panel (a) of Fig. 12, legend FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21; FCC_A1 rises to a flat 1.00 mol plateau (roughly 800–1050 °C) then falls to about 0.75 mol at 1300 °C; BCC_A2 vanishes near 750 °C; KAPPA_E21 near 0.20 mol falls to zero by about 800 °C.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 9Al-20Mn-1C composition (9 wt% Al, 20 wt% Mn, 1 wt% C, balance Fe); temperature range 0–1300 °C; y-axis 'Amount of all phases [mol]'.
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD equilibrium phase-fraction (amount of all phases vs temperature) calculation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used qualitatively: the calculated austenite (FCC_A1) fraction reaches a ~1.00 mol plateau over roughly 800–1050 °C and BCC_A2/KAPPA_E21 fall to zero near 750 °C and ~800 °C, i.e. austenite is more stable at 800 °C than at 1150 °C — consistent with the absence of austenite transformation observed for this composition at 800 °C.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Vickers hardness of 9Al-20Mn-1C: 233 HV hot-rolled, 359 HV after 600 °C tempering and 249 HV after 800 °C tempering (Table 8), i.e. the 800 °C state is harder than hot-rolled but markedly softer than the 600 °C tempered state; the same table ranks 9Al-10Mn-1C highest.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloyed steel produced by casting in a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots.
Ingots hot-rolled at 1150 °C to obtain 5 mm flat-products, followed by water quenching (parent process of this sample).
Samples heat treated at 800 °C for 30 min, followed by water quenching — the defining treatment of this sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers macro-hardness; 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: through-thickness embedded, ground and polished samples

structures.overall_structure: Predominantly retained austenite / no transformation: for the 9Al-20Mn-1C composition the austenite fraction (and therefore stability) is higher at 800 °C than at 1150 °C, so no cellular transformation or spinodal decomposition was detected after 800 °C tempering (contrast with the 12Al grades).

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-20Mn-1C alloy tempered at 800 °C is not covered by any dedicated micrograph in the paper; for this composition/condition only the hardness value (249 HV, Table 8) and the thermodynamic austenite-stability argument (Fig. 12(a)) are reported.

Per the conclusions, tempering at 800 °C in general triggered complete and widespread transformations such as cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition, but for the 9Al-20Mn-1C composition the austenite is more stable at 800 °C than at 1150 °C, so no such transformation was detected — reactions involving the austenite volume at 800 °C were reported only for the 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C grades.

The grain-striation and κ + α (and/or M3C) grain-boundary precipitate observations attributed to 9Al-20Mn-1C (Figs. 10(a) and 11; hardening at 600 °C without detectable austenite transformation, Table 8) pertain to the 600 °C tempered state, NOT to this 800 °C sample, and are therefore not assigned to this sample's structure/property fields.

At 800 °C the CALPHAD equilibrium for 9Al-20Mn-1C gives BCC_A2 = 0 mol (vanishes near 750 °C) and KAPPA_E21 = 0 mol (vanishes by ~800 °C) while FCC_A1 ≈ 1.00 mol, supporting an essentially fully austenitic equilibrium state.
The paper states that raw/processed data cannot be shared at this time (data are confidential and part of an ongoing study), so no additional quantitative data are available for this sample.
